title: perf(canary): automated latency/throughput regression detection and rollout guards
author: Priya Anand
description:
Context: We rely on continuous performance canaries to detect regressions before rolling changes to production. Previous canary logic flagged simple threshold breaches but produced noisy alerts and occasionally failed to stop rollouts when tail latency regressed under high throughput.

Summary: Introduces an automated canary detector with hysteresis-based rollout guards and adaptive threshold smoothing. The detector consumes per-route latency and throughput series, computes detection signals for 50/95/99/99.9 pcts and request/sec, and gates rollouts when regressions are confirmed by hysteresis and cross-metric correlation.

Changes include: new detector service (runtime/canary), config-driven thresholds and hysteresis windows, alerting rule templates, console dashboard panels, and an end-to-end perf canary test. No public API changes.

Checklist:
- [x] Detector algorithm implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Canary config schema + defaults added
- [x] Console dashboard and alert rules wired
- [x] E2E perf canary test added and passing in CI
- [x] Docs: README describing tuning knobs and incident playbook

Testing & validation: Ran perf canary e2e (synthetic traffic with injected 99th-pct regressions), verified detector catches >= 95% of injected regressions with < 3% false positives over 24h window. CI includes perf-canary-e2e job that ran on PR and passed.

Rollout plan: Squash-merge to main, staged rollout to canary namespace, monitor metrics and alerts for 48h, then promote to global canary. Playbook attached in README.

Related: Linear ENG-4281 (canary detector), ENG-4310 (rollout guard policy).
release_notes: Adds automated canary detector with hysteresis-based rollout guards and configurable thresholds. Improves detection sensitivity for 99th-pct latency regressions. No user-facing API changes.
